title: Payments release readiness
subject: Checkout 2.4 · RC3
scope: Payment capture, retry, and receipt paths on Chromium at 390px and 1440px
author: Coding agent
method: Source review, targeted Vitest run, and desktop/mobile browser smoke test

verdict.label: BLOCK RELEASE
verdict.headline: A retried capture can create a second charge before the release candidate ships.
verdict.next: Propagate the original idempotency key through retry, then rerun the timeout scenario twice.

summary: The normal payment path completes, but retry after a timeout is not idempotent.
The duplicate-capture behavior is reproducible and has a direct customer-billing impact.
Receipt rendering remains readable at the two inspected viewport widths.

sections.title: Decision context
paragraphs: RC3 is eligible to ship only if a retried capture maps to the original payment intent. The current implementation creates a fresh intent before entering the retry branch.
The review covers the supported checkout flow, not the unavailable live payment-provider replay environment.

sections.title: Payment path
paragraphs: The retry path branches after request timeout detection and calls capture creation with a newly generated idempotency key. The provider therefore treats the retry as a second payment intent.

sections.title: Receipt presentation
paragraphs: The receipt uses the existing table component and wraps long provider references without horizontal overflow. Both inspected viewport widths retained visible focus and readable evidence.

findings.title: Retry creates a fresh idempotency key
findings.observation: A capture retried after a client timeout can create a second provider payment intent.
findings.evidence:
retry.ts:41  const retryKey = createIdempotencyKey(paymentId)
retry.ts:47  return capture({ amount, idempotencyKey: retryKey })

targeted run: retry after timeout → PASS count 2, expected 1
findings.impact: A transient network failure can charge the customer twice.
findings.fix: Pass the original capture idempotency key into the retry branch and assert one provider intent across two attempts.

findings.title: Receipt remains readable at inspected widths
findings.observation: The receipt preserved table labels, focus visibility, and provider-reference wrapping at 390px and 1440px.
findings.evidence:
390×844 receipt: document.scrollWidth 390; focused reference outline visible
1440×1000 receipt: document.scrollWidth 1440; no clipped cells
findings.impact: Customers can inspect the final charge details on the supported desktop and mobile widths inspected.
findings.fix: Preserve the current wrapping assertion when changing the receipt table.

ran: npm test -- retry — 18 passed, 1 failed; failure reproduced twice
Opened file:///checkout at 390×844 and 1440×1000 — receipt and evidence remained readable
not_verified: Live payment-provider sandbox replay was unavailable
Firefox and Safari print previews were not inspected
